name: the Teskari
identity: Terrace-builders of the high mountains: tea growers, bellfounders and kite-flyers who carve stairways into cliffs.
architecture: Stone terraces stepping down every slope, tiled roofs that curl up at the corners like a smile, bell towers on the crags, and rope-and-plank bridges strung between peaks.

festivals.name: the Kite Ascent
festivals.description: Every family flies a kite painted with a wish. The highest kite wins nothing at all except a year of bragging.

festivals.name: Bellnight
festivals.description: At midnight every bell in the mountains rings once, peak after peak, until the sound has crossed the whole range.

festivals.name: Tea Moon
festivals.description: The first leaves of the year are tasted by moonlight on the highest terrace, and everyone pretends to notice the difference.

values: climbing a little higher each year
pride: Their bells, their tea, and bridges from the Lamplit Age that are still standing.

makersMarks: a tiny bell engraved where the hand rests
the number of steps from the maker's door, in old Teskari script
a kite-shaped seal in red wax

relations.note: The yearly Peak Race, and an old argument over whose horns and bells carry farther.
Teskari tea and slate go down to the red country; Ochrel glass and dyes come up.
Their best customers for tea, though the Wendle brew it far too strong.
